editorial.titleTr: Column: Ruling Party's Discord Deepens Rift With Public as "Impeachment Signals" Emerge
summaryTr: The ruling party leader has even mentioned 'signs of impeachment,' intensifying internal strife.
The president's declining approval rating stems not from weakened reform efforts, but from failures in state governance.
Unilateral policies that disregarded common sense and fairness have caused the public to lose trust.
editorial.bodyTr:
Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok said yesterday that internal party criticism of President Lee Jae-myung resembles "a prelude to the situation when outside and inside forces joined together to impeach President Roh Moo-hyun." He was expressing frustration with hardliners within the party who emphasize only the clarity of reform. Earlier, Gyeonggi Province Governor Choo Mi-ae criticized the nomination of a prosecutor-turned candidate for major crimes investigator, saying she is "anxiously on edge, relying on forces of sedition." Former Democratic Party leader Jung Chul-kyou said on Kim Eo-jun's broadcast that "the president was stabbed in the back by the prosecution." While it is concerning that the ruling party's leader in the second year of administration would use the word "impeachment," revealing acute factional conflict, the bigger problem is that both sides are barking up the wrong tree.

President Lee's declining approval ratings are not primarily due to dispersed party strength or weakened clarity of reform causing core supporters to defect. The primary reason is that the common sense, fairness, and pragmatic centrist approach that President Lee has emphasized in state affairs have disappeared without a trace. The ruling party's legislative actions, the government's policies, and the presidential office's personnel appointments have been a succession of arrogance that ignores public common sense. The administration abolished supplementary investigative authority without providing any measures for crime victims, while implementing real estate tax reforms that increase tax burdens on non-resident homeowners. Current real estate policy turns most public office candidates in the August 30 cabinet reshuffle into speculators. Yong Hye-in, the nominee for minister of gender equality and family affairs, who became a proportional representative lawmaker through a trick satellite party and refused to give up concurrent positions, ultimately stepped down to shield Kim Seung-won, the justice minister nominee facing more serious allegations. Suspicions surrounding Kim's involvement in new drug lobbying continue to reveal circumstances that endanger the lives and property of the people through human trials and stock price manipulation. Through a series of these incidents, presidential job approval ratings have fallen for nine consecutive weeks, reaching 33.8 percent according to Realmeter as of yesterday. In party support ratings, the Democratic Party at 36.1 percent has fallen behind the People Power Party at 42.1 percent. What is happening back and forth within and outside the party is not because the intensity of reform is weak or its purity has been tarnished, nor because different factions within the camp have obstructed reform, but rather is a result of the people's disappointment with state governance itself. The only way to win back the departed public support is to realize the people's common sense in reality.

editorial.title: Vetting failure
editorial.body: Flawed nominees pass scrutiny while ruling party reduces confirmation hearings to hollow exercise Rep. Yong Hye-in's resignation as nominee for Minister of Gender Equality and Family is ultimately the result of Cheong Wa Dae's vetting failure. Yong did not even make it to the National Assembly's confirmation hearing. The ruling Democratic Party of Korea did not even schedule a confirmation hearing for her, and its leader, Kim Min-seok, reportedly went so far as to send his chief of staff to urge her to step down. Her firm stance that she would retain her seat as a sitting proportional-representation lawmaker while also serving as a minister — an unprecedented move in Korea's constitutional history — appeared highly self-serving to the public. Furthermore, new evidence emerged suggesting that she had turned the party she belonged to into a personal fiefdom, intensifying the criticism against her. Although the ruling party moved to contain the fallout by having her resign voluntarily, the ultimate responsibility lies with Cheong Wa Dae, which failed to anticipate that Yong would insist on holding both a ministerial post and her proportional-representation seat in the National Assembly. Kim Seung-won, the nominee for justice minister whose confirmation hearing begins today, is also a vetting failure on par with Yong. Nevertheless, the Democratic Party of Korea appears to be doing everything it can to protect him. Party leader Kim Min-seok fueled public anger by saying of Kim Seung-won's nomination, "The more I look into it, the more I believe it was a good appointment. I will stand by it." The level of public criticism of Kim Seung-won is such that some argue he should be subject to a special counsel investigation rather than a confirmation hearing. However, Kim Min-seok effectively made clear that the party's position was to adopt the confirmation hearing report on Kim Seung-won, regardless of critical public opinion. Kim Seung-won's confirmation hearing is expected to be a hollow exercise that will effectively deprive the public of the opportunity to vet the nominee. That is intended to shield him from mounting public criticism. The Democratic Party rejected all the witnesses requested by the opposition People Power Party for the confirmation hearings of all the nominees, not just Kim Seung-won. Seo Young-kyo, a Democratic Party lawmaker who chairs the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, came up with the sophistry that a normal confirmation hearing is one in which the minister nominee himself serves as the witness and no other witnesses are present. The close relationship between Kim Seung-won and a broker surnamed Yang, the relationship among Kim, Yang and the judge who at the time rejected an arrest warrant for the largest shareholder of a company developing a new drug, and stock-price manipulation linked to clinical trial approval were all potentially fatal liabilities for Kim’s qualifications to serve as a minister. Yet Kim passed the vetting process and was nominated as a ministerial candidate. These were all matters that Cheong Wa Dae should have been able to find out. If Cheong Wa Dae failed to uncover these flaws in the vetting process, it was incompetent; if it knew about them and still nominated Kim, it is guilty of dereliction of duty and of arrogance and self-righteousness toward the public. It must have a system in place to select qualified candidates and filter out potential risks through cross-checking. The ruling party's use of its parliamentary majority to push through confirmation hearings in which it rejected the opposition's requests for witnesses and allowed the nominees to do nothing but offer their own defenses is an affront to the public. If an unqualified person becomes a minister through a meaningless confirmation hearing, the public will be the only ones to suffer. Confirmation hearings, too, must restore their original function of assessing nominees' qualifications and moral character. editorial.bodyTr: 용혜인 성평등가족부 장관 후보자 사퇴는 결국 청와대의 인사검증 실패의 결과다. 용 후보자는 국회 인준청문회에도 도달하지 못했다. 여당인 더불어민주당은 인준청문회 일정조차 잡지 않았고, 김민석 당대표는 자신의 비서실장을 보내 사퇴를 종용한 것으로 알려졌다. 현직 비례대표 의원 신분을 유지하면서 동시에 장관을 맡으려는 태도는 한국 헌정사에 전례 없는 것으로, 국민에게 매우 자기중심적으로 비쳤다. 더욱이 자신이 속한 정당을 개인의 영토로 만들었다는 새로운 증거가 나오면서 그에 대한 비판이 심해졌다. 여당이 자발적인 사퇴를 유도해 피해를 최소화했지만, 궁극적인 책임은 용 후보자가 장관직과 비례대표 의원직을 모두 유지하겠다는 입장을 예상하지 못한 청와대에 있다. 오늘부터 인준청문회가 시작되는 김승원 법무부 장관 후보자도 용혜인과 맞먹는 수준의 인사검증 실패다. 그러나 더불어민주당은 그를 보호하기 위해 모든 수단을 다하고 있는 것으로 보인다. 김민석 당대표는 김승원 후보자 지명에 대해 "살펴볼수록 좋은 인사라는 생각이 든다. 끝까지 함께하겠다"고 말해 국민의 분노를 자극했다. 김승원 후보자에 대한 국민의 비판 수준은 인준청문회보다는 특별검사 대상이 되어야 한다는 주장까지 나올 정도다. 그럼에도 김민석은 공개 여론에 관계없이 김승원 후보자의 인준청문회 결과를 수용하겠다는 당의 입장을 사실상 명확히 했다. 김승원 법무부 장관 후보자의 인준청문회는 국민에게 피청문인을 검증할 기회를 사실상 박탈하는 공허한 형식이 될 것으로 예상된다. 이는 국민의 비판으로부터 그를 보호하려는 의도다. 더불어민주당은 김승원뿐만 아니라 모든 후보자의 인준청문회에서 국민의힘이 요청한 증인을 모두 거부했다. 입법사법위원회 위원장을 맡은 민주당의 서영교 의원은 정상적인 인준청문회는 장관 후보자 본인만 증인으로 참석하고 다른 증인은 없는 것이라는 궤변을 제시했다. 김승원과 양 모 중개인의 관계, 김과 양, 그리고 당시 신약 개발 회사 대주주의 영장 기각 결정을 내린 판사 사이의 관계, 임상시험 승인과 연결된 주가조작 의혹 등은 모두 장관직 적격성에 치명적일 수 있는 사항들이었다. 그럼에도 김승원은 검증 과정을 통과했고 장관 후보자로 지명됐다. 이 모든 것은 청와대가 충분히 파악할 수 있어야 했던 사항들이다. 청와대가 검증 과정에서 이런 결함을 발견하지 못했다면 무능이고, 이를 알면서도 여전히 김을 지명했다면 직무유기이자 국민에 대한 오만과 자기중심성이다. 청와대는 유능한 인물을 선발하고 교차검증을 통해 잠재적 위험 요소를 걸러낼 수 있는 시스템을 갖춰야 한다. 여당이 국회에서의 다수당 지위를 이용해 야당의 증인 요청을 거부하고 후보자들이 자신의 항변만 펼칠 수 있도록 한 인준청문회는 국민에 대한 모욕이다. 형식적인 인준청문회를 통해 부적격자가 장관이 되면 결국 고통받는 것은 국민이다. 인준청문회도 후보자의 적격성과 도덕성을 평가하는 본래의 기능을 회복해야 한다.

editorials.title: Vetting failure
editorials.body: Flawed nominees pass scrutiny while ruling party reduces confirmation hearings to hollow exercise Rep. Yong Hye-in's resignation as nominee for Minister of Gender Equality and Family is ultimately the result of Cheong Wa Dae's vetting failure. Yong did not even make it to the National Assembly's confirmation hearing. The ruling Democratic Party of Korea did not even schedule a confirmation hearing for her, and its leader, Kim Min-seok, reportedly went so far as to send his chief of staff to urge her to step down. Her firm stance that she would retain her seat as a sitting proportional-representation lawmaker while also serving as a minister — an unprecedented move in Korea's constitutional history — appeared highly self-serving to the public. Furthermore, new evidence emerged suggesting that she had turned the party she belonged to into a personal fiefdom, intensifying the criticism against her. Although the ruling party moved to contain the fallout by having her resign voluntarily, the ultimate responsibility lies with Cheong Wa Dae, which failed to anticipate that Yong would insist on holding both a ministerial post and her proportional-representation seat in the National Assembly. Kim Seung-won, the nominee for justice minister whose confirmation hearing begins today, is also a vetting failure on par with Yong. Nevertheless, the Democratic Party of Korea appears to be doing everything it can to protect him. Party leader Kim Min-seok fueled public anger by saying of Kim Seung-won's nomination, "The more I look into it, the more I believe it was a good appointment. I will stand by it." The level of public criticism of Kim Seung-won is such that some argue he should be subject to a special counsel investigation rather than a confirmation hearing. However, Kim Min-seok effectively made clear that the party's position was to adopt the confirmation hearing report on Kim Seung-won, regardless of critical public opinion. Kim Seung-won's confirmation hearing is expected to be a hollow exercise that will effectively deprive the public of the opportunity to vet the nominee. That is intended to shield him from mounting public criticism. The Democratic Party rejected all the witnesses requested by the opposition People Power Party for the confirmation hearings of all the nominees, not just Kim Seung-won. Seo Young-kyo, a Democratic Party lawmaker who chairs the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, came up with the sophistry that a normal confirmation hearing is one in which the minister nominee himself serves as the witness and no other witnesses are present. The close relationship between Kim Seung-won and a broker surnamed Yang, the relationship among Kim, Yang and the judge who at the time rejected an arrest warrant for the largest shareholder of a company developing a new drug, and stock-price manipulation linked to clinical trial approval were all potentially fatal liabilities for Kim’s qualifications to serve as a minister. Yet Kim passed the vetting process and was nominated as a ministerial candidate. These were all matters that Cheong Wa Dae should have been able to find out. If Cheong Wa Dae failed to uncover these flaws in the vetting process, it was incompetent; if it knew about them and still nominated Kim, it is guilty of dereliction of duty and of arrogance and self-righteousness toward the public. It must have a system in place to select qualified candidates and filter out potential risks through cross-checking. The ruling party's use of its parliamentary majority to push through confirmation hearings in which it rejected the opposition's requests for witnesses and allowed the nominees to do nothing but offer their own defenses is an affront to the public. If an unqualified person becomes a minister through a meaningless confirmation hearing, the public will be the only ones to suffer. Confirmation hearings, too, must restore their original function of assessing nominees' qualifications and moral character. The approval rating reflects government legitimacy and the nation's capacity to govern.

editorials.titleTr: [Editorial] Is the Mega Special Zone Act's 'Holding Company Deregulation' Simply a Tailor-Made Favor for SK?
summaryTr: Government and ruling party's mega special zones law includes relaxed regulations on holding companies
Concerns arise over conglomerates' concentrated economic power and allegations of tailored favoritism for specific groups
Questions raised over whether selective benefits are being targeted at SK Group
editorials.bodyTr:
The government and the Democratic Party of Korea are set to introduce a special law on designating and managing "mega special zones" this month, and it has been revealed that the bill includes provisions to relax regulations on holding companies. This has sparked concerns about economic concentration among conglomerates and controversy over "customized preferential treatment" for specific groups. According to a comprehensive review of Hankyoreh's reporting, the ruling party and government are reportedly planning to include in the mega special zone law provisions that would allow holding companies to increase their stake in subsidiaries beyond current limits and expand opportunities for circular investment among affiliates.

This move is raising red flags among observers who worry it could further entrench the dominance of large conglomerates in the Korean economy. Critics argue that relaxing restrictions on holding company structures would primarily benefit a small number of major conglomerates, particularly those with complex cross-shareholding arrangements, and effectively amount to handpicking advantages for specific corporate groups rather than pursuing neutral, across-the-board economic policy.

The controversy highlights an ongoing tension in South Korea's economic policy between efforts to promote growth and innovation through deregulation and concerns about maintaining fair competition and preventing excessive wealth concentration among a handful of powerful business families. As lawmakers prepare to debate the mega special zone legislation, the inclusion of holding company regulatory relief has become a focal point for broader questions about whose interests such policies ultimately serve.
